findings.F1: The tested effect sits almost entirely in the earlier years. In the trending regime (90-day return above 0), the slope of the demeaned 5-day return on the close's position in its 30-day range is +0.068 (t 4.65, 689 grid cases) over 2018–2021 and +0.001 (t 0.10, 623 cases) over 2022–2025. By year, 2020 alone has t 4.80, and 2022–2025 each have |t| < 0.6.
findings.F2: The tested effect is uneven across coins. The trending range-position slope is positive with t 1.83–2.75 for XRPUSD, ZECUSD, BTCUSD and ETHUSD, but −0.008 (t −0.30, 203 cases) for LTCUSD and +0.011 (t 0.58, 234 cases) for XMRUSD.
findings.F3: In the unknown regime (90-day return at or below 0), strength reverses after 2021. Over 2022–2025 the slope of the demeaned 5-day return on the 20-day return in units of 20-day daily volatility is −0.0158 (t −4.55, 721 cases), and on the 30-day range position it is −0.030 (t −2.96, 654 cases). Over 2018–2021 the same slopes are +0.0072 (t 1.65) and +0.030 (t 2.15), so the pooled slope is only −0.0037 (t −1.33).
findings.F4: Inside the trending regime, recent strength of any length precedes more rise over the next 5 days. Slopes of the demeaned 5-day return: 1-day return in volatility units 0.0094 (t 3.15), 5-day 0.0087 (t 2.86), 20-day 0.0096 (t 3.33), over 1549 / 1549 / 1465 cases. The same slopes in the unknown regime have |t| ≤ 1.33.
findings.F5: In the trending regime, the 5-day move is lopsided across range quintiles. The top range quintile is followed by +1.14 % demeaned (t 1.99, 495 cases) and the second-lowest by −1.44 % (t −2.39, 186 cases). The unknown regime shows no quintile with |t| > 0.6.
findings.F6: Saturdays stand out. The cross-coin mean Saturday return is +0.45 % (t 3.04, 414 days), the largest of the 7 weekdays, and Saturday minus other days is positive in 7 of 8 years, though no single year passes t 1.63 on day means. This is a weekday condition, not a graded situation, so no idea is drawn from it.
findings.F7: The book's gain comes from long holds and long trades:

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 90-day return is negative, the larger its 20-day return measured in units of its daily volatility, the more it falls over the next 5 days, and the deeper it has fallen the more it rises back.
ideas.consequence: A trader would refuse to chase a sharp 20-day bounce in a coin still down over 90 days, and would lean against it.
ideas.name: bounce fades in fallers

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 90-day return is positive, the larger its last day's return measured in units of its daily volatility, the more it rises over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy into, not fade, a strong up-day in a coin rising over the past 90 days.
ideas.name: risers' strong days continue
